observations: Photo 0: a used petrol car engine, inline four cylinder, out of a vehicle and standing on a concrete floor in a parts yard.
Four ignition coil packs on top of a black plastic valve cover, oil filler cap, black plastic intake manifold, wiring loom and hoses still attached.
Green spray paint marks across the top of the engine, the kind of yard marking used on imported used engines.
Alternator and belt pulley visible at the lower right; dust and grime on the cover and harness.
A faint watermark is across the photo but is not legible; no maker's logo, engine code or serial is readable.
Another engine is visible behind it; people's feet at the edges.

read_from: photo 0 shape only: inline four cylinder engine with coil packs and plastic intake; no maker or engine code readable

claims.evidence: No Hyundai or Kia logo, engine code or part number is readable in photo 0; the layout fits many makers.
Photo 0 shows a used, dusty engine with yard spray paint marks, standing on the floor of a parts yard.
Seals and bolts are not shown close up; a still photo cannot prove the engine was never opened.
No clip of the engine running, no compression test.
No receipt or warranty document is shown.

risks.risk: Engine is not the model or maker claimed, or is a different displacement or code than the buyer's car needs.
risks.proof: Sharp close-up of the engine code and serial stamped on the block.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced for a specific vehicle; identity stays unknown.

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage: low compression, knocking, burnt valves, worn timing chain.
risks.proof: Clip of the engine running on a stand or in a car, plus a compression test reading on each cylinder.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, for parts.

risks.risk: Cracked block or head, missing parts on the sides not shown.
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides and the underside of the engine.

risks.risk: Receipt and warranty do not exist or do not belong to this engine.
risks.proof: Photo of the receipt and warranty showing the same engine serial as the block.

proof_requests: Close, sharp photo of the engine code and serial number stamped on the block.
Clip of the engine running, with sound.
Photos of every side of the engine, including the underside and the sump.
Photo of the receipt and warranty card carrying the engine serial.
response.reason: Photo 0 shows a used inline four cylinder petrol engine, but no maker, engine code or serial is readable, and the price of an engine is set by its exact code and fitment. The engine code must be shown before even a worst case price is possible.
